You are a programming expert. 
        You will be provided with a patch used to fix a bug. 
        Based on the commit message and modifications in the patch, you need to analyze the root cause of the bug in detail. 

        Here is the patch content:
        From 64598e23de7873b9d47cd9b9a02daa2bb4ded343 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Dan Carpenter <dan.carpenter@oracle.com>
Date: Sat, 3 Jul 2021 12:46:20 +0300
Subject: [PATCH] drm/amdgpu: return -EFAULT if copy_to_user() fails

If copy_to_user() fails then this should return -EFAULT instead of
-EINVAL.

Fixes: c65b0805e77919 ("drm/amdgpu: RAS EEPROM table is now in debugfs")
Signed-off-by: Dan Carpenter <dan.carpenter@oracle.com>
Reviewed-by: Luben Tuikov <luben.tuikov@amd.com>
Signed-off-by: Alex Deucher <alexander.deucher@amd.com>
---
 drivers/gpu/drm/amd/amdgpu/amdgpu_ras_eeprom.c | 4 ++--
 1 file changed, 2 insertions(+), 2 deletions(-)

diff --git a/drivers/gpu/drm/amd/amdgpu/amdgpu_ras_eeprom.c b/drivers/gpu/drm/amd/amdgpu/amdgpu_ras_eeprom.c
index 3e33e85d8dbc..d2e5b2567bc1 100644
--- a/drivers/gpu/drm/amd/amdgpu/amdgpu_ras_eeprom.c
+++ b/drivers/gpu/drm/amd/amdgpu/amdgpu_ras_eeprom.c
@@ -771,7 +771,7 @@ amdgpu_ras_debugfs_eeprom_size_read(struct file *f, char __user *buf,
 	res = min_t(size_t, res, size);
 
 	if (copy_to_user(buf, &data[*pos], res))
-		return -EINVAL;
+		return -EFAULT;
 
 	*pos += res;
 
@@ -950,7 +950,7 @@ amdgpu_ras_debugfs_eeprom_table_read(struct file *f, char __user *buf,
 		res = min_t(size_t, res, size);
 
 		if (copy_to_user(buf, &data[*pos], res))
-			return -EINVAL;
+			return -EFAULT;
 
 		*pos += res;
 
-- 
2.25.1


        
        Provide a response strictly in the following format:
        Root cause:<Root cause>

Root cause: The bug was caused by the incorrect error code being returned when the `copy_to_user()` function failed. Instead of returning `-EINVAL`, which indicates an invalid argument, the function should return `-EFAULT`, which indicates a bad address error. This misclassification of the error could lead to improper handling of the failure in the calling code, potentially causing further issues in the system.

You are a programming expert.
    You will be given the root cause of a bug and  the corresponding patch.
    You need to extract the code statements that lead to the bug from  the patch, based on the root cause.

    <text1>
